objective: Distinguish operative transaction or term status from the status of the available document so corpus answers exclude unsupported proposals without requiring an executed copy in every case.

changes.failure_pattern: The always-visible corpus protocol categorically demoted lifecycle status to a non-gating attribute, so proposed, abandoned, or never-applicable items entered affirmative populations even when the request presupposed an operative transaction or term.
changes.mechanism: Require lifecycle meaning to be inferred from the whole request and independently record substantive applicability and document-copy status, keeping proposal-only ambiguity outside affirmative counts.
changes.rationale: The earliest shared error occurs during request-gate construction before search, so the always-visible system workflow must remove the harmful universal rule.

evidence: attribution/C7/transition.json: chg-2b partially effective but status calibration remained incomplete
changes.failure_pattern: Candidate ledgers and final audits conflated whether a transaction or term became operative with whether an executed or final document copy was available.
changes.mechanism: Add separate substantive-state and document-state fields, verb- and context-sensitive lifecycle tests, boundary handling for proposals, and a candidate-level precision audit requiring corroboration of operative facts.
changes.rationale: C7's detailed gate skill was partially effective and should be improved rather than discarded; the registered skill is the reusable surface for the candidate-level evidence protocol.
